title: Model Watchtower: enterprise-fit signal ops & prioritized research runway
creator: Diego Morales
description: Build an operational 'Model Watchtower' that continuously ingests public model releases, benchmark signals, and customer voice to score enterprise fit and trigger tactical research work. This ticket scopes the initial MVP: signal sources, scoring rubric, a lightweight dashboard, and a prioritized research runway (3-month backlog) for PM + Applied ML to evaluate high-risk/high-opportunity models.
background: We get ad-hoc model signals from community threads, partner newsletters, and field asks. Sales and Solutions teams report bursts of interest in new open weights or quantization techniques without a consistent triage or prioritization flow. This causes reactive model onboarding requests and missed GTM opportunities. The Watchtower standardizes signals, correlates them with customer-vector metrics, and creates a repeatable research intake.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented signal taxonomy and ingestion plan (sources, freshness, owners) is approved by PM and Applied ML.
- An automated pipeline prototype that pulls metadata from 3 sources (Hugging Face model registry RSS, selected research Twitter handles, and our internal field spreadsheet) runs daily.
- A scoring rubric (enterprise-fit) with 5 factors (latency footprint, license risk, quantization readiness, feature parity, ecosystem integrations) implemented in a spreadsheet and validated on 10 candidate models.
- A lightweight dashboard (Confluence + embedded chart or internal dashboard link) showing ranked candidates and the top-5 research tasks in runway.
- A prioritized 12-week research backlog with owners and success criteria for top 3 items.
research_findings: Surveyed 40 field notes (sales/solutions) and identified three recurring enterprise requirements: deterministic latency, explicit licensing clarity, and HSM/KMS integration guidance.

Preliminary scan (Feb 2026) identified 7 new model releases with enterprise-relevant traits: low-precision checkpoints, modular tokenizer changes, or permissive licensing.
- 2 models appear promising for cost-focused inference (low KV-cache footprint).
- 1 model requires legal review due to dual-license ambiguity.
Community adoption velocity correlates with early adapter performance blog posts and packaged inference scripts; models without packaging rarely surface in field asks.
next_steps: ENG: Stand up a daily ingestion job (minimal scraper) for 3 sources and write outputs to shared CSV (owner: Priya Rao, ENG-22041).
PM: Finalize enterprise-fit scoring rubric and run a pilot evaluation on 10 models (owner: Ava Chen).
Applied ML: Triage top-3 candidates and define experimental success criteria (owner: Dr. Marcus Lee).
Design: Prototype dashboard wireframe for signal surfacing and research runway visualization (owner: Lina Park).
Legal: Quick license triage for top-5 candidates (owner: Rachel Kim).
risks: Signal noise: high false positives from community chatter could waste research cycles.
Dependency on ENG scraper: limited SRE capacity may delay reliable ingestion.
License ambiguity: legal blockers could stop enterprise adoption even for strong technical fits.
Over-indexing on novelty: prioritizing new models that don't yield unit-cost improvements for production.
monitoring_metrics: Weekly new candidate volume (unique models ingested)
Time-to-triage (days from ingestion to initial PM score)
Number of customer escalations referencing non-supported models (monthly)
